title: Companion accepted decisions and trade-offs

approval.statement: Go with all the recommended decisions
approval.scope: The four recommendations in the preceding trade-off review, including its revised scope and saving recommendations.

implementation_status: planned; no application implementation is recorded as complete
interpretation: Implementation requirements below make the accepted behavior concrete. They describe obligations and safeguards for the future spec. Open questions remain unapproved choices and must not be silently treated as settled.

decisions.title: Deliver the complete capture-to-project workflow first
accepted_decision: Include quick capture, a daily inbox, automatic Reel to MD intake, one MyTune project brief, Codex idea chat, and explicit saving to the Obsidian vault.
Use a reel-to-MyTune conversation that produces a cited experiment proposal as the first acceptance scenario.
Include a small paired comparison of direct brainstorming and explicit analogy reasoning in this milestone.
Deliver watches and the formal repeated, blind-scored evaluation in later increments.
decisions.rationale: A complete journey tests whether the product helps turn collected material into a useful project idea. An early paired comparison tests the central reasoning technique before extensive product work.

costs: Does not test project relevance or the value of the reasoning workflow
alternatives.disposition: Deferred as a standalone release boundary. These capabilities remain the first implementation steps.

alternatives.option: Complete workflow with all comparison work deferred
benefits: Less evaluation work during the first milestone
costs: Delays evidence about whether explicit analogy adds value
alternatives.disposition: Rejected in favor of a small early paired comparison.

alternatives.option: Full draft including watches and formal evaluation
benefits: Covers the broad product vision together
costs: Adds background matching, lifecycle state, deduplication, and evaluation tooling before core usefulness is established

consequences: Several integrations must work before the first complete acceptance scenario can pass.
A weak idea may result from source quality, retrieval, project context, or reasoning. The workflow must expose enough evidence to distinguish those causes.
A small comparison provides exploratory evidence. It cannot establish general usefulness or learning outcomes.
The first milestone includes both an explicit analogy path and a direct brainstorming path for comparison.

implementation.requirement: Provide thought/link capture and a Today inbox backed by vault notes. Capture and import must remain usable when Codex is unavailable.

Detect completed intake artifacts, validate the supported export contract, and create or update a capture with visible success or failure. Partial writes and unreadable input must not appear as successful imports.
Build one MyTune brief from selected current project documents, retaining source references and the context version used for a conversation.

Support a conversation using selected captures and the MyTune brief. The analogy output must explain the shared mechanism, project application, limitations, and a small test, with references to both source and project context.
Allow an explicit no-useful-connection result. Label proposed applications as hypotheses and expose missing support.

Provide a paired comparison using the same source material, project brief, model, candidate count, and approximately comparable generation budget. Record prompts, model, inputs, outputs, and comparison conditions. Rate usefulness, surprise, grounding, and ease of testing using the same rubric. Include a case where analogy may add little.

Implement in verifiable steps. Establish capture/import first, then project context and a real signed-in Codex interaction, then saving and the paired comparison. Use fixture responses for repeatability and a real interaction for integration evidence.

acceptance_checks: With a test vault and supported reel export, import once, discuss its application to MyTune, and explicitly save a cited experiment proposal that opens in Obsidian.
Re-importing the same logical export leaves one current capture.
Offline or unavailable Codex does not prevent capture/import or damage existing notes.
A non-fit example can finish without a proposal.
Run both comparison paths on identical material and retain the conditions and outputs for inspection.

decisions.title: Manage imported content and preserve user writing separately
accepted_decision: Keep one current imported capture per logical export.
Re-imports update export-owned content and metadata.
Store user annotations and saved ideas in separate linked notes.
Retain enough revision information to identify the evidence used by an existing proposal.
Carry identity, revision, provenance, and review information through an explicit import contract.
decisions.rationale: Separate ownership permits predictable import updates while preserving user writing. Revision-aware citations let an older proposal remain inspectable after its source changes.

alternatives.option: Replace an unrestricted editable imported note
costs: Can destroy user edits

alternatives.option: Managed and editable sections in one note
benefits: Source and commentary stay together in Obsidian
costs: Marker changes and concurrent edits make safe updates more complex

alternatives.option: Create a new inbox note for every import
costs: Creates duplicates and complicates identifying the current capture
alternatives.disposition: Rejected as the inbox model. Evidence history may still be retained outside the current inbox entry.

consequences: Related content spans multiple notes, so the interface must make navigation and joint reading easy.
Imported notes are managed content even though users can access them in Obsidian.
Conflict handling is required when a user edits a managed note externally.
Current capture content and historically cited evidence have distinct lifecycles.
Validated export, review decision, and factual support must remain distinguishable.

implementation.requirement: Resolve a logical export identity independently from its path and revision identity. Retry or relocation must not create a second current capture for the same export.

Validate an import envelope carrying logical identity, revision identity, content, available source locators/timestamps, provenance, and review information. Do not infer human approval from a successful export or a content completeness field.
Update only the managed capture. Link annotations and saved ideas using a stable capture identity so import updates do not break their relationship.

Make import publication atomic from the user's perspective. Detect changed destination content before replacing it and preserve conflicting user content. A failed or retried import must leave a recoverable state.

Record the source revision and evidence location used by each saved idea. Make that cited revision inspectable after a later import using D06 immutable snapshots. O02 tracks retention and deletion details.
Show source content, annotations, linked ideas, and review information together or through direct navigation. Explain the ownership of managed notes before direct editing.
Preserve original captures. Saving an interpretation or experiment creates its own note and does not rewrite the source to agree with the proposal.

acceptance_checks: Import revision A, add an annotation and saved idea, then import revision B. There is one current capture, user writing is intact, and the old idea's evidence from A remains inspectable.
Retry an interrupted import without duplicates or false success.
Modify a managed note in Obsidian before re-import. Preserve the edit and expose a recoverable conflict.
An export without human review remains visibly unreviewed. An unreadable review bundle does not silently become reviewed.
Move an input file while keeping its logical export identity and verify deduplication.

decisions.title: Distinguish captures, project briefs, saved ideas, and experiment proposals
accepted_decision: A Capture is collected material for possible later use, with an initial type of thought, link, or reel import.
A Project Brief supplies project goals and constraints.
A Saved Idea records an interpretation or conclusion developed from material.
An Experiment Proposal is a saved idea that includes a testable hypothesis and a proposed test.
Today is a date-filtered view of captures. Older captures remain accessible.
Several captures can support one idea, and one capture can support several ideas.
decisions.rationale: A shared inbox accommodates different inputs while explicit concepts keep source material, project context, and generated interpretation understandable.

alternatives.option: Call every stored item a capture
costs: Blurs collected evidence, project context, and interpretation

alternatives.option: Use unrelated concepts and lists for each capture type
costs: More terminology and repeated behavior across browsing and search

consequences: Capture types need different metadata and rendering while sharing inbox behavior.
An imported capture can have provenance that a rough thought lacks.
Older material needs navigation beyond Today.
Relationships between captures and ideas must support multiple links in both directions.
An experiment proposal is a specialization of a saved idea, so the app must not require a test for every saved idea.

implementation.requirement: Represent stable capture identity, type, captured time, content, and available provenance. Use type-specific metadata for imports without requiring invented source metadata on a rough thought.
Keep source occurrence time, import time, and captured time distinct when available. Apply D11 first-capture semantics to Today. O10 tracks timezone and day-boundary details.
Provide access to earlier captures and connected ideas. Changing the day must not delete, resolve, or hide older captures from all navigation.
Represent source-to-idea links as many-to-many relationships and retain the relevant evidence revision. Keep project context references distinguishable from capture references.
Treat Experiment Proposal as a saved idea with experiment fields. Avoid mandatory experiment fields for other saved ideas.

acceptance_checks: Create a thought, a bare link, and a reel import. Each appears as a capture with its type and available metadata.
Find a capture from a previous day.
Save an idea using two captures, then save another idea from one of those captures. Navigate all relationships.
Save an idea without an experiment and a complete experiment proposal without misclassifying their supporting captures.

decisions.title: Save structured ideas explicitly, with experiments when ready
accepted_decision: Saving a note requires an explicit user action.
Show the proposed note and vault destination before committing it.
Save a structured idea containing an explanation, supporting references, and explicit uncertainty.
Include an experiment when the idea has a hypothesis, a small test, and an observable result.
The first acceptance scenario must produce a complete experiment proposal.
Retain conversation history locally under D13 independently from explicitly saving notes.
decisions.rationale: Explicit saving keeps the vault deliberate. Flexible structured ideas preserve useful conclusions at different stages, including a conclusion that a proposed analogy fails.

benefits: Low effort and fewer forgotten ideas
costs: Adds weak suggestions, duplicates, and conversational debris

alternatives.option: Automatically save candidate drafts for later promotion
benefits: Preserves candidates with a later quality gate
costs: Adds another inbox and lifecycle
Can omit evidence and the reason the idea mattered
alternatives.disposition: Rejected as the default saved artifact.

alternatives.option: Require an experiment for every save
costs: Forces premature experiments and excludes useful observations

consequences: Users can leave without saving useful material.
Preview and explicit commit add an interaction.
Incomplete ideas and missing support must be representable honestly.
Saved notes and conversation history require separate persistence policies.
A failure to save must remain recoverable without creating duplicate notes on retry.

implementation.requirement: Provide a save action that builds a proposed standalone note and shows its content and destination. Commit only after the explicit save confirmation.
Include a title, explanation, source/project references where available, and uncertainty or limitations. Clearly disclose missing support rather than generating citations.

When an experiment is present, include the hypothesis, borrowed mechanism, project application, smallest test, and observable result. Validate completeness before labeling the note an Experiment Proposal.
Retain capture identities, cited revisions, evidence locations, and project context references in the saved artifact. Distinguish source claims from proposed applications.
Write the note safely, avoid overwriting unrelated files, and make retries recoverable without duplicate successful saves. Preserve the proposed content after failure so the user can retry.
Handle a useful negative conclusion such as an analogy breaking down as a normal Saved Idea. A no-useful-connection response does not require a saved artifact.
Apply D13 local history and restart/resume behavior independently from explicit note saving. Set remaining retention, storage, and recovery details through O12.

acceptance_checks: Generate a useful idea and verify that it becomes a vault note only after an explicit save confirmation.
Review note content and destination before writing.
Save an observation with no test and an explanation of a failed analogy.
Save a complete experiment proposal with source and project citations, then open it in Obsidian.
Simulate a failed write and retry. Recover the content and produce one successful note.
Update a cited capture after saving and verify that the saved idea still identifies its original evidence.

decisions.title: Admit valid draft and reviewed exports
accepted_decision: Automatically admit valid draft exports and reviewed exports, preserving their distinct status.
A partial but valid draft may enter the inbox and inform a conversation. Show review status, limitations, and evidence together.
Failed processing and incomplete file transfers are outside successful imports.
Preserve actual human review decisions and findings.
decisions.rationale: Admission before formal review makes the inbox useful earlier.

costs: Delays access to useful draft material
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

alternatives.option: Treat all exported material as equally trusted
costs: Hides uncertainty and review findings
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: Conversations must handle uncertain source material explicitly.
A validated export is not proof that every claim is correct.

implementation.requirement: Validate supported artifacts before publishing an import. Separate processing completeness, validation, extraction uncertainty, and human review information.
Expose status and limitations both in the capture view and in context sent to Codex.
Do not label incomplete transfers, failed processing, or unreadable review metadata as a successful reviewed import. The exact handoff and contract remain open.

acceptance_checks: A valid partial draft appears as unreviewed with its limitations.
A reviewed import preserves the decision and findings.
An incomplete transfer or failed artifact is not admitted as successful.

decisions.title: Retain immutable imported text revisions in the vault
accepted_decision: Keep an immutable text-and-metadata snapshot of every successfully imported revision inside the vault.
Keep one current capture and revision history outside the daily inbox. Saved ideas refer to the revision used.
Snapshots retain imported text, evidence references, provenance, and review metadata.
Reference original videos through available locators.
decisions.rationale: Historical evidence stays inspectable when the current capture changes.

costs: Earlier cited evidence can disappear
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

costs: Greater storage and asset management burden
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: Additional files and storage are accepted.
Text retention cannot guarantee future access to an original video.
Cleanup and deletion policies remain unresolved.

implementation.requirement: Publish an immutable snapshot for every accepted imported revision while preserving the current capture identity.
Store source text and metadata with revision identity and evidence anchors. Keep snapshots accessible from citations and outside Today.
Resolve a saved idea's evidence link to its cited revision after an update. Detect snapshot damage and report unavailable evidence rather than substituting newer text.
Do not infer authorization to copy original videos. Store their available locators. Retention and deletion behavior require O02.

acceptance_checks: Import A, cite A, import B, and open both A and B independently.
Retry A without an extra accepted snapshot.
An unavailable video is reported while retained text remains accessible.

decisions.title: Send visible bounded context to Codex
accepted_decision: Send the user's question, relevant conversation history, and a bounded selection of capture and project excerpts to Codex.
Companion assembles the context and makes included sources visible.
Allow inspection and removal of included sources before sending.
Direct agent access to vault and project folders is outside the initial workflow.
decisions.rationale: Explicit source selection supports hosted reasoning with an inspectable data boundary.

costs: Broader exposure and harder-to-bound reads
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

alternatives.option: Require all content to remain on the PC
costs: Conflicts with using hosted Codex inference on those contents
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: Selected content leaves the PC.
Bounded context can omit relevant material.
Retrieval quality and source selection are Companion responsibilities.
Integration and effective access controls still require verification.

implementation.requirement: Build each outgoing context package in Companion with selected excerpts, provenance, and relevant history.
Present included sources and support removing them before dispatch. Send only the reviewed package after the user's send action.
Keep vault and project folders outside direct agent tool access and test the effective boundary on Windows.

Expose unavailable authentication, offline operation, usage limits, interruption, and other failed turns while preserving local capture and existing notes. Set exact context bounds and integration through O03/O06.

acceptance_checks: Remove a source before sending and verify its text is excluded from the outgoing context, including reintroduced history.
Verify bounded context and visible sources correspond to the actual outgoing package.
Attempt an agent read outside supplied context and verify it cannot read vault/project folders.
Simulate an interrupted turn without losing local captures.

decisions.title: Approve project brief refreshes and pin conversation context
accepted_decision: Build the MyTune brief from an explicitly selected set of current project documents.
Generate a proposed brief with references and require user approval.
Detect changed inputs and offer a reviewed refresh before the next conversation.
An existing conversation retains the brief version it started with.
Allow continuing with a visibly outdated brief.
decisions.rationale: Reviewed versions preserve user control and make conversations reproducible.

costs: Changes the basis of reasoning without review
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

costs: Context drifts from the project
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: Brief approval adds an interaction.
The user may continue with visibly outdated context.

implementation.requirement: Record selected documents and their versions with each proposed brief and retain source references.
Require approval to activate a newly generated or refreshed brief.
Detect changes to selected inputs and offer a new brief before starting a conversation; visibly mark outdated inputs.
Pin the approved brief version when starting a conversation and preserve access to the cited context. Resolve missing inputs, limits, and refresh failures through O04.

acceptance_checks: Change an input document and verify a refresh is offered without silently replacing the active brief.
An existing conversation retains its original brief while a new conversation can use an approved refresh.
Continuing with an older brief shows it is outdated.

decisions.title: Pause per-capture updates on managed note conflicts
accepted_decision: Preserve an externally edited managed capture and pause its updates until the user resolves the conflict.
Preserve both the local version and the incoming revision.
Offer to move user changes into an annotation and then apply the update, or leave the conflict unresolved.
Other imports continue.
While unresolved, identify the version used by a conversation.
decisions.rationale: Explicit conflict resolution preserves writing without guessing how to merge source material.

costs: Loses user writing
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

costs: Can alter source meaning or annotations
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

alternatives.option: Stop all intake on one conflict
costs: Unrelated imports are blocked
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: Updates for the conflicting capture are interrupted.
Conflicts may remain unresolved and conversations need explicit version identity.

implementation.requirement: Detect destination changes against the last managed version before applying an update.
Preserve local and incoming content and mark the capture conflicted. Continue independent intake.
Present local changes for user-controlled transfer to an annotation before applying the incoming revision.
Keep unresolved conflicts recoverable across restart and identify the exact content used in any conversation. Resolve rename/deletion/concurrency details through O07.

acceptance_checks: Edit a managed note, re-import, and verify both versions survive.
Import an unrelated capture during a conflict.
Resolve into an annotation and verify the user content and new source are both retained.
Restart during an unresolved conflict and recover its state.

decisions.title: Use a dedicated structured vault folder
accepted_decision: Use one dedicated folder inside the selected vault, with separate areas for captures, annotations, ideas, project briefs, and revision history.
Let the user choose the parent folder during setup.
Use stable item identities in metadata, readable filenames, and ordinary Markdown links.
Renames and moves must preserve identity and relationships.
decisions.rationale: A visible ownership boundary makes storage and recovery understandable.

alternatives.option: Scatter notes through existing vault folders
costs: Harder to identify managed content and recover relationships
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

alternatives.option: Keep all artifacts in one flat folder
costs: More clutter and less clear ownership
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: More files and folder structure appear in Obsidian.
Exact folder names, metadata, link repair, and lifecycle behavior remain to be settled.

implementation.requirement: Set up an explicit user-selected parent folder with distinct artifact areas.
Persist stable item identities independently from paths and readable filenames.
Use ordinary Markdown links and reconcile identity when notes move or are renamed.
Keep managed content ownership clear and avoid overwriting unrelated notes. Determine schema and repair rules through O09.

acceptance_checks: Create each artifact type under the selected parent folder.
Open notes and relationships in Obsidian.
Rename or move a note and preserve its identity and relationships.
Encounter an unrelated filename collision without overwriting it.

decisions.title: Base Today on the first capture date
accepted_decision: Today shows material first captured into Companion during the current local calendar day.
Importing an old reel today puts it in Today.
A later update retains the original capture date.
Keep source date and revision time separately when available.
Older captures remain accessible through history and search, and updates need a separate visible indicator.
decisions.rationale: The view answers what the user collected today.

costs: Newly imported old material disappears from Today
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

costs: Blurs collection date and refresh date
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: Updates do not automatically re-enter Today.
Timezone changes and day-boundary details require an explicit follow-up policy.

implementation.requirement: Store the initial capture time immutably and preserve it across imports and revisions.
Filter Today using the capture time and local calendar day under the selected timezone policy.
Store source and revision times separately and surface an update indicator.
Maintain historical browsing/search. Set travel, timezone changes, and backdating rules through O10.

acceptance_checks: Import an old reel and find it in Today.
Update it on the next day and verify its initial capture date is retained.
Show the update separately and locate the capture in history.

decisions.title: Keep quick capture minimal and offline
accepted_decision: Accept a thought or link without a required title, project, or tags.
Save entered text locally and assign its capture time.
Derive an editable display title.
Reject empty input.
Store pasted links immediately and make fetching content an explicit later action.
decisions.rationale: Minimal input reduces capture friction and works offline.

costs: More friction when capturing a fleeting idea
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

costs: Network dependency, latency, and unintended fetching
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: Titles and initial organization can be uneven.
Stored links have no searchable page content until explicitly enriched.

implementation.requirement: Provide thought/link entry with no mandatory organization fields.
Validate nonempty text and persist it locally with capture time without waiting for Codex or a network request.
Derive a display title that the user can edit without changing capture identity.
Keep links as entered and require explicit fetching. Specify entry shortcuts and enrichment behavior through O11.

acceptance_checks: Capture text and a link while offline.
Reject empty input without creating an item.
Edit a derived title and preserve the capture identity.
Paste a link and verify no page fetch occurs automatically.

decisions.title: Retain resumable conversations locally
accepted_decision: Automatically retain chat history locally so conversations can resume after app closure.
Retain messages and source/brief revisions used by each turn.
Show interrupted replies as interrupted.
Allow deleting a conversation independently of saved ideas.
Vault idea notes continue to require explicit saving.
decisions.rationale: Local history reduces lost thinking and supports finding prior exploration.

costs: Loses context and unsaved thinking
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

alternatives.option: Save each conversation as an idea note
costs: Blurs exploratory dialogue and deliberately saved ideas
alternatives.disposition: Not selected for the initial workflow.

consequences: Sensitive local history and storage growth are accepted.
Conversation deletion has a separate lifecycle.
Storage location, retention, and history-search behavior remain unresolved.

implementation.requirement: Persist messages, per-turn context references, and turn completion/interruption state locally.
Resume locally retained history after restart without presenting an interrupted response as complete.
Support explicit conversation deletion without deleting independent saved ideas.
Do not create a saved idea merely because conversation history was retained.
Set retention, provider-side thread behavior, removed-source handling, and historical search through O12/O06.

acceptance_checks: Restart after a completed turn and restore the conversation with its context references.
Restart during a reply and show its interrupted state.
Delete a conversation and verify an explicitly saved idea remains.
Retain a conversation without creating an idea note.

decisions.title: Reconcile intake on a 24-hour schedule

approval.statement: Make it some kind of cron job which checks every 24 hours. Otherwise go with the recommendation.
approval.question: Q14

accepted_decision: Check selected Reel to MD draft and optional finalized-review folders every 24 hours.
Import eligible validated drafts and finalized reviewed material regardless of whether the user clicked Export Markdown.
Validate artifacts before admission and persist processed identities.
Use a scheduled reconciliation rather than continuous watching or frequent polling.
decisions.rationale: The user explicitly chose a 24-hour cron-like check while accepting the remaining intake recommendation.

costs: More background activity and does not meet the selected cadence
No automatic intake and no producer download receipt

consequences: Material may wait up to the next daily check.
A supported scheduler and a missed-run policy are required.
The initial or manual scan, closed-app behavior, and catch-up policy remain open.

implementation.requirement: Configure explicit draft and optional review roots and reconcile on a persisted 24-hour schedule.
Admit drafts only after validated readiness and reviews only after bundle validation and the applicable review policy.
Persist artifact identities and outcomes so repeat runs do not duplicate captures or snapshots.

Preserve the user's 24-hour cadence. Do not silently retain the earlier startup-plus-periodic recommendation. Specify scheduler registration, missed runs, overlap, first scan, and manual checks through O13.

acceptance_checks: With a controlled clock, verify scheduled checks are 24 hours apart under the selected scheduling policy.
An eligible artifact is imported on a scheduled run without requiring browser download.
Repeat a reconciliation without duplicate captures or snapshots.
Invalid or partially written artifacts remain outside successful imports.

decisions.title: Group identical source bytes and prefer reviewed revisions

approval.statement: For all the other questions go with the recommendations.
approval.question: Q15

accepted_decision: Identical source-video bytes normally map to one capture using the source hash to connect processing attempts.
Keep each accepted revision.
Reviewed current material is not automatically replaced by a later unreviewed draft.
Resolve competing reviewed revisions explicitly when their relationship is ambiguous.
Different video bytes start separate captures unless the user explicitly links them. Different processing settings remain revision history.
decisions.rationale: A conservative identity policy avoids accidental merges and preserves reviewed context.

costs: Moves and copies can duplicate a source
A draft or ambiguous finalization can replace reviewed material
Can merge distinct clips without evidence

consequences: Re-encoded or edited copies may need manual linking.
Ambiguous reviewed revisions require user resolution.
Source hashes identify identical bytes, not semantic equivalence.

implementation.requirement: Map processing attempts to capture identity using verified source hashes when available.
Record attempts and finalizations as distinct revision identities while applying reviewed-over-draft precedence.
Detect ambiguous reviewed successors and request an explicit current revision choice without discarding either revision.
Require explicit user linking for different source bytes. Define missing hashes, manual linking, and legacy artifacts through O01.

acceptance_checks: Reprocess identical video bytes under a different configuration and retain one capture with revision history.
Import a draft after a reviewed revision and preserve the reviewed current revision.
Import competing reviewed revisions and preserve both pending a user choice.
Import re-encoded bytes as a separate capture until explicitly linked.

approval.statement: For all the other questions go with the recommendations.
approval.question: Q16

accepted_decision: Automatic context discovery initially searches Companion-managed captures, annotations, saved ideas, and approved project briefs.
Other vault notes become sources only through explicit inclusion.
Selecting a vault does not enroll every personal note in automatic discovery.
decisions.rationale: An explicit corpus boundary makes discovery understandable and limits accidental inclusion.

alternatives.option: Automatically index the whole selected vault
costs: Enrolls personal notes without a separate selection

alternatives.option: Require manual source selection for every turn
costs: More repeated work and weaker automatic discovery

consequences: Existing Obsidian notes may remain undiscovered until included.
Retrieval methods, bounds, and inclusion lifecycle still need definition.

implementation.requirement: Maintain an explicit eligible corpus based on managed artifact types and separately included vault notes.
Exclude unapproved brief drafts and unselected personal notes from automatic discovery.
Provide an explicit action to include another vault note as a source.
Apply eligibility before ranking and context assembly. Define index, ranking, and historical search through O06.

acceptance_checks: Search for a phrase present only in an unselected vault note and verify it is absent from automatic discovery.
Include that note and verify it can be discovered.
Verify approved briefs are eligible and unapproved refresh drafts are excluded.

decisions.title: Retain material until explicit deletion and warn about dependencies

accepted_decision: Retain notes, snapshots, and conversations until explicitly deleted. Start without automatic expiry.

Treat conversation deletion independently from saved ideas.

decisions.title: Separate completeness, uncertainty, and human review judgments

approval.statement: For all the other questions go with the recommendations.

accepted_decision: Show processing completeness, extraction uncertainty, and human review as separate fields.
Preserve actual human review decisions and available claim-level findings.
Make rejected reviews visible against the existing capture and exclude rejected material from automatic supporting evidence.
Prompt review of ideas that depend on rejected material.
decisions.rationale: Separate judgments avoid a misleading single trust badge.

costs: Conflates completeness, extraction quality, and human findings
Obscures evidence changes affecting existing ideas

consequences: Status display is more detailed.
Dependent ideas need explicit handling when support is later rejected.
